prediction.raw: 0. As a Christian, you may consider the principles of fairness, honesty, and reciprocity. In this scenario, you used your company gas card to fill up the tank on the way to the destination, which means you didn't directly pay for it yourself. However, you still provided the gas, which is a valuable contribution to the trip. Your friend's argument that it didn't count because you didn't pay for it yourself seems unfair, as the end result is that you still supplied half the gas. Additionally, considering that you used your car for the last trip and this was his turn to provide the vehicle, it seems reasonable that you wouldn't have to pay for half the gas on the way back. It's also worth considering the spirit of sharing expenses and being a good friend. If you had paid for the gas yourself, your friend would likely have reimbursed you for half. The fact that you used a company gas card doesn't change the fact that you provided a valuable resource for the trip. Ultimately, it seems that you are not in the wrong (NTA) for not directly paying your friend for half of the gas used on the trip.
